action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions targeting ES|QL multi-valued field aggregation semantics and SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging. Questions decompose requirements using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (aggregation intent), pain points (error clarity, result accuracy), acceptance criteria (diagnostic capability), and prioritization (error message vs. auto-fix vs. docs). Chain-of-thought reasoning identified three core concerns: (1) semantic clarity around null contributions in computed fields, (2) error message specificity for unbounded sorts, (3) user expertise and operational context.

Interview questions designed to elicit user goals (multi-value aggregation semantics), pain points (unbounded SORT errors, unclear messaging), and acceptance criteria (error message specificity, MV_EXPAND+LIMIT requirement clarity) using 5W1H and Socratic techniques grounded in ES|QL requirement fragments.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (aggregation semantics, error clarity), pain points (confusing error messages, unbounded sort failures), and acceptance criteria (error message quality, documentation needs) for ES|QL multi-value field handling and SORT+MV_EXPAND constraint communication.

End users require explicit, command-specific error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts and transparent null-handling documentation for multi-valued field aggregations to reduce debugging time and improve query reliability in ES|QL analytics workflows.

End users require explicit error messaging that identifies command combinations (SORT+MV_EXPAND) causing unbounded operations, and transparent null-handling semantics for multi-valued field aggregations to prevent silent failures and accelerate query debugging in analytical workflows.

ES|QL users require explicit error messaging for SORT + MV_EXPAND conflicts and transparent null-handling semantics for multi-valued field aggregations to prevent silent data loss and accelerate query debugging in production analytics environments.

Five clarification questions raised regarding multi-valued field aggregation semantics (NULL handling in computed expressions), error message specificity for SORT+MV_EXPAND failures, and consistency of multi-value behavior across ES|QL operations.

EndUser raises five clarification questions addressing: (1) consistency of null-handling across aggregation functions for multi-valued computed expressions, (2) treatment of null values in sum calculations, (3) error message design philosophy (prescriptive vs diagnostic), (4) whether multi-valued field exclusion is intentional feature or limitation, and (5) whether MV_EXPAND-specific error messaging is necessary or generalizable.

Six clarification questions raised regarding multi-valued field computation semantics, aggregation function consistency, null-handling in results, error message design for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts, scope of error improvements, and user-facing documentation strategy. These questions address ambiguities in requirement fragments about expression evaluation on multi-valued fields and error messaging specificity.

Confirmed core multi-valued field aggregation semantics: computed expressions exclude multi-valued documents, returning NULL contributions. Refined SORT+MV_EXPAND error messaging to explicitly identify both commands and prescribe fixes. Clarification needed on LIMIT placement direction in error remediation guidance.

End user confirmed multi-valued field expression behavior (NULL return, document exclusion from aggregations) and refined SORT + MV_EXPAND error messaging to explicitly diagnose the command conflict and prescribe remediation. All clarifications on null-handling uniformity and aggregation function scope resolved. Requirements validated for elasticsearch_2026q1 implementation.

End-user confirmed multi-valued field aggregation semantics (computed expressions return NULL for multi-valued documents, excluded from aggregations) and refined error messaging for SORT+MV_EXPAND conflicts to be explicit and prescriptive. All clarifications resolved; requirements ready for deployer validation.

Consolidated 5 structured elicitation records addressing ES|QL multi-valued field aggregation semantics and error messaging. Core requirements: (1) computed expressions on multi-valued fields return NULL and exclude documents from aggregations; (2) STATS operations apply mixed-value rules consistently; (3) SORT+MV_EXPAND error messages explicitly diagnose root cause and prescribe fixes; (4) null-handling remains transparent and uniform across functions. All records aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability and validated against enduser confirmations.

Five prioritized user requirements synthesized from elasticsearch_2026q1 case addressing multi-valued field aggregation semantics (MUST: 3 items covering expression null-handling, SUM calculation consistency, and error message clarity), documentation and cross-function consistency (SHOULD: 2 items), and progressive error messaging (COULD: 1 item). All requirements traced to validated enduser confirmations and existing requirement records. MoSCoW prioritization applied using life-cycle trade-off reasoning: MUST items block core functionality; SHOULD items reduce user friction; COULD item enhances UX.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing infrastructure constraints (query execution environment, error surfacing mechanisms), security mandates (compliance logging, error message information disclosure), and scalability expectations (multi-valued cardinality impact, SORT+MV_EXPAND detection latency, backward compatibility, adoption growth). Applies 5W1H and Socratic techniques to decompose deployment feasibility and operational risk of enhanced error messaging and multi-valued aggregation semantics.

Probed 8 targeted questions addressing infrastructure capacity for multi-valued aggregations, security/audit implications of null-handling, version compatibility constraints, observability requirements for error detection, documentation synchronization, computational overhead of SORT+MV_EXPAND validation, downstream tool integration risks, and user migration/communication strategy. Chain-of-Thought reasoning: decomposed requirements REQ-ES-2026Q1-001 through -005 into deployment-phase concerns spanning scalability, security, operational visibility, and change management to ensure error message refinement and null-handling semantics are feasible and sustainable in production.

Eight targeted questions probe Deployer constraints across infrastructure (cluster topology, query throughput, latency SLAs), security (data classification, audit logging), scalability (user expertise tiers, memory footprint), and deployment (backward compatibility, documentation rollout) to ground the error message enhancement and multi-valued field aggregation requirements in operational reality.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for multi-valued field aggregation semantics and SORT+MV_EXPAND error enhancement. Requirements demand: (1) query-time unbounded detection in ES|QL parser, (2) document-level cardinality metadata at indexing, (3) O(n) aggregation pipeline processing, (4) <5ms validation latency, (5) non-breaking minor-version deployment with synchronized documentation, (6) stateless coordinator-node query rejection, and (7) performance regression testing across multi-valued prevalence scenarios. All constraints align with Elasticsearch scalability and security posture.

Deployer confirms infrastructure requirements for pre-execution unbounded sort detection, document-level cardinality discrimination during aggregation, enhanced error messaging with sanitization, and operational documentation for multi-valued field semantics. Scalability targets <5ms planning latency and sub-linear AST analysis complexity. Security mandates prevent internal topology exposure. Operational procedures standardize error formats and document multi-valued aggregation behavior consistently across all functions.

Deployer confirms infrastructure requirements for unbounded sort detection at query planning stage (<5ms), document-level cardinality metadata for multi-valued field discrimination, security-compliant error messaging (user-facing command names only), and scalability targets maintaining sub-100ms query latency. Operational procedures standardize error message format and document multi-valued aggregation semantics. Cost-performance trade-off prioritizes indexing-time cardinality metadata to reduce query execution overhead.

Six clarifications needed on infrastructure implementation details: cardinality detection timing (index vs. query), AST analysis placement (compile vs. execute), error message structure (unified vs. dual-path), null-handling mechanism (document vs. expression vs. field level), security boundary scope (command names vs. positions vs. fields), and AST caching strategy (key/invalidation/sizing). These resolve gaps between high-level requirements and deployment constraints around performance, security, and scalability.

Deployer requires clarification on five operational constraints: (1) field cardinality detection timing and cost trade-off (index vs. query-time), (2) unbounded sort detection placement relative to query planning/execution stages and <5ms SLA feasibility, (3) error message prescriptiveness scope (unified vs. separated diagnostic/prescriptive outputs), (4) null-handling consistency across aggregation functions beyond SUM, and (5) security boundaries for exposing query structure in error messages. These clarifications directly impact infrastructure design, scalability targets, and security compliance.

Six clarification requests raised by Deployer role targeting infrastructure constraints, security boundaries, and cost-performance trade-offs. Issues span: (1) cardinality detection timing/cost strategy, (2) query planning vs. execution stage for unbounded sort detection, (3) error message prescriptiveness scope and latency impact, (4) multi-valued aggregation processing location (distributed vs. centralized), (5) security boundary for error message content, (6) field metadata tagging cost model. All questions require explicit trade-off analysis per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deployment checklist before implementation can proceed.

Deployer confirms and refines three core requirements: (1) multi-valued field computed expressions return NULL and exclude multi-valued documents from aggregations uniformly across all functions; (2) STATS aggregations process single vs. multi-valued documents per documented semantics (SUM(X)=18, SUM(X+a)=7 example validated); (3) SORT + MV_EXPAND error message refined to explicitly diagnose conflict and prescribe fix. Resolved deployer clarifications: index-time cardinality detection for <5ms runtime performance; pre-execution AST analysis for early error messaging; security constraints enforced (no internal plan exposure). All requirements align with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deployment checklist and scalability SLA targets.

Deployer confirms three core requirements: (1) multi-valued field expressions return NULL and exclude documents from computed aggregations; (2) STATS SUM(X), SUM(X+a) produces 18,7 result; (3) SORT + MV_EXPAND error message explicitly identifies conflict with prescriptive fix. Resolves two deployment trade-offs: index-time vs. query-time cardinality detection (recommend index-time for <5ms SLA), and query planning vs. execution stage for unbounded sort detection (mandate pre-execution AST analysis). Requires field metadata tagging, security-compliant error messaging, and comprehensive user documentation.

Deployer confirms three core requirements: (1) Multi-valued field computed expressions return NULL with consistent null-handling across aggregation functions; (2) STATS SUM(X), SUM(X+a) produces 18,7 result through dual-path aggregation logic; (3) Enhanced SORT+MV_EXPAND error message explicitly identifies conflict and prescribes fix. Deployment strategy: implement index-time cardinality metadata tagging (~2% storage cost), dual-path aggregation processor, and pre-execution AST-based unbounded sort detection (<5ms SLA). No infrastructure blockers. Security and scalability requirements satisfied.

Elasticsearch 2026Q1 operating environment requires: (1) Hardware: AST query analysis engines with <5ms latency and sufficient memory for document-level cardinality tagging; (2) Network: Early error signaling at query planning stage with security constraints (no internal topology exposure); (3) Compliance: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 documentation standards for multi-valued field semantics; (4) Software: Lightweight AST-based unbounded sort detection, document-level cardinality discrimination in aggregation pipelines, and enhanced error messaging (diagnostic + prescriptive) for SORT + MV_EXPAND conflicts; (5) Deployment: Clarification needed on index-time vs. query-time field cardinality metadata strategy to optimize storage vs. compute trade-offs while maintaining sub-100ms query latency SLA.
